content.text:
What kind of story is The Elves and the Shoemaker?

The Elves and the Shoemaker is the warm tale of little elves who secretly help a poor shoemaker night after night, and the elderly couple who repay that kindness. It's a Brothers Grimm story that teaches children diligence along with gratitude and giving back.

content.alt: The Elves and the Shoemaker - The original story
content.text:
The original story

The original is "The Elves and the Shoemaker (Die Wichtelmänner)" from the Brothers Grimm collection. While a poor shoemaker sleeps, tiny elves make perfect shoes for him, and once his fortunes improve, the elderly couple sews small clothes for the elves to show their thanks.

content.alt: The Elves and the Shoemaker - Plot summary
content.text:
Plot summary

On a night when the poor shoemaker has leather left for only a single pair, tiny elves appear and make splendid shoes. As the shoes sell well and his fortunes improve, the elderly couple makes small clothes and shoes as a gift for the elves, who looked cold. The elves leave overjoyed, and the couple lives happily ever after.

content.alt: The Elves and the Shoemaker - The moral
content.text:
The moral of this tale

The heart of it is a diligent heart in work, and a heart that gives thanks and repays the help it receives. Talk with your child about how help isn't one-way—it grows even warmer when it's given and received.

content.alt: The Elves and the Shoemaker - How to read it aloud
content.text:
How to read it aloud

Read the night scenes of the elves at work in a mysterious, small voice, and the couple's scene of thanks warmly. Ask "If someone secretly helped me, how would I repay them?" to lead into a spirit of gratitude. Best suited for ages 4-7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is this story best for?
A. It's best for ages 4-7. With the warm themes of help, giving back, and gratitude, it's great for emotional development.

Q. What is the original title?
A. It's the Brothers Grimm's "The Elves and the Shoemaker (Die Wichtelmänner)." In Korea it's affectionately called "The Old Shoemaker and the Little Elves."

Q. What activities pair well with it?
A. Making a thank-you card, "thinking of people who have helped me," and drawing a small gift all work nicely.
